## What STITCH is about

::: {.wide}
Science is increasingly done in teams, yet we still evaluate it as if it were the work of individuals. **STITCH** (*Scientific Teams and InequaliTies: Collaboration and Heterogeneity in Science*) looks inside research teams to understand how work is divided, how this varies across fields, and how that division shapes careers and inequalities by **gender, geography and career stage**.

We combine sociology of science, bibliometrics and data science, starting from a large collection of publications with contribution statements (CRediT). The goal is evidence that helps build fairer ways of recognising and evaluating collective work.
:::
::: {.aims}
::: {}
<span class="aim-n">01</span>

**Map** how scientific teams organise their work across fields.
:::
::: {}
<span class="aim-n">02</span>

**Follow** how teams and roles change over time.
:::
::: {}
<span class="aim-n">03</span>

**Uncover** the inequalities built into who does what.
:::
:::
